clauses: For a three-player standard game, aliens are selected.
Which flares enter the cosmic deck.
How many cards each player receives.
How the first player is selected.

answer.text: For a three-player standard game, aliens are selected.
answer.answer: Each player gets two flares and their matching alien sheets, secretly chooses one alien and returns the other sheet; this same setup applies in a three-player game.

answer.text: Which flares enter the cosmic deck.
answer.answer: Both flares dealt to each player enter the deck, including the rejected alien’s flare; add random extras if needed to reach ten total.

answer.text: How many cards each player receives.
answer.answer: Each player is dealt an eight-card hand.

answer.text: How the first player is selected.
answer.answer: Draw destiny until a player color appears; that player starts. Shuffle that card back into destiny. Turns then pass left.

clauses: What counts as one colony.
Whether several players can have colonies on one planet.
Whether five foreign colonies must be in different systems.

answer.text: What counts as one colony.
answer.answer: A colony is one or more ships of a single color on one planet; extra same-color ships there do not create extra colonies.

answer.text: Whether several players can have colonies on one planet.
answer.answer: Yes. Several colors can coexist on the planet, each with its own colony.

answer.text: Whether five foreign colonies must be in different systems.
answer.answer: No. Five foreign colonies may all be in one other system.

clauses: Whether offense must retrieve a warp ship when available at Regroup.
Where the original rulebook places the retrieved ship when offense has colonies or none.

answer.text: Whether offense must retrieve a warp ship when available at Regroup.
answer.answer: Yes. Offense must retrieve one ship from the warp if available.

answer.text: Where the original rulebook places the retrieved ship when offense has colonies or none.
answer.answer: With an existing colony, place it on any existing home or foreign colony. The original rulebook says to put it directly in the gate if offense has no colonies. Separately, the FAQ permits a player with no colonies or ships on their turn to place it on any home planet.

clauses: What happens when only one destiny card remains.
Choices after drawing own color when the home system contains a foreign colony.
Choices after drawing own color when there is a completely empty home planet.

answer.text: What happens when only one destiny card remains.
answer.answer: Do not draw that last card. Shuffle it together with the destiny discards, then draw from the new deck.

answer.text: Choices after drawing own color when the home system contains a foreign colony.
answer.answer: Redraw, or target one chosen foreign colony in your home system; its owner becomes defense and other colonies there are bystanders.

answer.text: Choices after drawing own color when there is a completely empty home planet.
answer.answer: Instead, offense may target a home planet with no ships of any color and move up to four ships from any of its other existing home or foreign colonies onto it, reclaiming it automatically.

clauses: Whether offense may attack Blue’s foreign colony in Red’s home system after drawing Blue without a special power.
Who defends Red’s empty home planet if foreign bystanders are present.

answer.text: Whether offense may attack Blue’s foreign colony in Red’s home system after drawing Blue without a special power.
answer.answer: No. Ordinarily Blue’s color directs the encounter to Blue’s home system; offense cannot attack a foreign colony in a third player’s system.

answer.text: Who defends Red’s empty home planet if foreign bystanders are present.
answer.answer: The owner of the home system, Red, defends that planet even with zero ships on it. Other colors’ colonies are bystanders: they add nothing to defense and are unharmed by the result.

clauses: From where and how many ships offense may launch.
Whether offense may strip a colony.
Whether defense may add or subtract ships on the target during Launch.

answer.text: From where and how many ships offense may launch.
answer.answer: Offense chooses one planet in the destiny-indicated system and launches one to four ships from any combination of its existing home and foreign colonies, placing them on the gate’s wide end.

answer.text: Whether offense may strip a colony.
answer.answer: Yes. It may remove the last ship, which immediately eliminates that colony; returning ships cannot restore that now-empty location as though it remained a colony.

answer.text: Whether defense may add or subtract ships on the target during Launch.
answer.answer: No. Defense cannot add or subtract ships on the target.

clauses: Order of invitations and commitments.
Whether someone invited by both sides can join both.
Where defensive allies place ships.

answer.text: Order of invitations and commitments.
answer.answer: Offense names invitees first; defense then names invitees. Starting left of offense and proceeding clockwise, each other player accepts one invitation or declines all, then commits ships before the next decides.

answer.text: Whether someone invited by both sides can join both.
answer.answer: No. A player may join only one side or neither.

answer.text: Where defensive allies place ships.
answer.answer: Each joining ally contributes one to four ships from any of their colonies. Defensive allies place ships beside the target planet, not on it. (For effects referring to the gate, FAQ treats those defensive allies as in the gate.)

clauses: Which side wins given attack 10 plus six offensive ships versus attack 12 plus four defensive ships.
What happens to offense and offensive allies.
What happens to defense, defensive allies and bystanders.

answer.text: Which side wins given attack 10 plus six offensive ships versus attack 12 plus four defensive ships.
answer.answer: Totals are offense 10 + 6 = 16 and defense 12 + 4 = 16. Defense wins the tie.

answer.text: What happens to offense and offensive allies.
answer.answer: Their ships go to the warp.

answer.text: What happens to defense, defensive allies and bystanders.
answer.answer: Defending and bystander colonies stay. Defensive allies return their committed ships to any existing own colonies, including different origins. Bystanders survive.

clauses: Where ships on each side go when offense wins an attack.
Whether existing bystander colonies survive.
Whether reinforcing an existing colony earns another colony.

answer.text: Where ships on each side go when offense wins an attack.
answer.answer: All offense and offensive ally ships land on the target, establishing or reinforcing their respective color colonies. Defense and defensive ally ships go to the warp.

answer.text: Whether existing bystander colonies survive.
answer.answer: Yes. Bystanders survive.

answer.text: Whether reinforcing an existing colony earns another colony.
answer.answer: No. Advance a colony marker only for a newly established foreign colony, not a reinforcement.

clauses: Number and choices of rewards for a defensive ally contributing three ships to a winning defense.
Where the ally’s committed ships and retrieved ships go.

answer.text: Number and choices of rewards for a defensive ally contributing three ships to a winning defense.
answer.answer: The ally must receive one defender reward per contributed ship: three total. For each, it may draw one cosmic-deck card or retrieve one of its warp ships to any own colony, mixing the reward types freely; it may not decline. It must declare its full mix before taking any reward and may not inspect an initial draw before deciding the remaining sources.

answer.text: Where the ally’s committed ships and retrieved ships go.
answer.answer: The ally returns its committed ships to any existing own colonies (they may have different origins). Each retrieved warp ship goes to any own colony.

clauses: Compensation amount for the main player’s three own ships actually lost to warp, excluding two allied ships.
Source and selection of the compensation cards.
What happens if the opponent has fewer than three cards.

answer.text: Compensation amount for the main player’s three own ships actually lost to warp, excluding two allied ships.
answer.answer: Compensation is three cards, one for each of that main player’s own ships actually lost to the warp. The two allied losses do not count.

answer.text: Source and selection of the compensation cards.
answer.answer: The losing main player takes the cards from the opponent’s hand at random, without seeing their faces (card backs may be seen).

answer.text: What happens if the opponent has fewer than three cards.
answer.answer: Take the opponent’s entire hand if it has fewer cards than the compensation owed.

clauses: What happens to allies when both main players reveal negotiate.
Time limit and permitted exchange between the main players.
Where a deal colony may be granted and which ships the recipient may use.
What makes a valid deal.
Failure penalty and ordinary second encounter eligibility.

answer.text: What happens to allies when both main players reveal negotiate.
answer.answer: Allies on both sides return their ships to their own colonies, gain nothing, and cannot participate in the deal.

answer.text: Time limit and permitted exchange between the main players.
answer.answer: The main players have one minute. They may transfer cards from their hands and/or grant colonies to each other.

answer.text: Where a deal colony may be granted and which ships the recipient may use.
answer.answer: A grant is one colony on a planet where the giver already has a colony, including a foreign colony. The recipient may use any of their own ships not in the warp; ships coexist, and the giver need not vacate.

answer.text: What makes a valid deal.
answer.answer: At least one card or colony must actually transfer; a deal may be one-sided and cannot be an agreement to do nothing. Tangible terms are limited to permitted cards/colonies and specific exceptions; future promises are unenforceable, and agreed card terms must be truthful and honored.

answer.text: Failure penalty and ordinary second encounter eligibility.
answer.answer: If time expires without agreement, each main player loses three ships of their choice to the warp, and offense cannot take an ordinary second encounter. A successful deal qualifies for an ordinary second encounter but is not a win for win-only powers.

clauses: What Morph copies and when.
Whether Morph tracks later changes to the opponent’s card.
What happens after the encounter.

answer.text: What Morph copies and when.
answer.answer: Morph becomes an exact copy of the opponent’s initially revealed encounter card; an attack copies its initial value, and a negotiate becomes a negotiate.

answer.text: Whether Morph tracks later changes to the opponent’s card.
answer.answer: No. Later modifications do not automatically carry over; Morph may be modified separately.

answer.text: What happens after the encounter.
answer.answer: Morph returns to its normal identity and is normally discarded with the other revealed encounter card, unless an effect changes its destination.

clauses: Who may play reinforcements and when.
Which side a reinforcement may affect.
When the reinforcement response window ends.

answer.text: Who may play reinforcements and when.
answer.answer: During Reveal, after encounter cards are revealed, either main player or any ally may play a reinforcement.

answer.text: Which side a reinforcement may affect.
answer.answer: It adds its printed amount to either side’s total, including the opposing side.

answer.text: When the reinforcement response window ends.
answer.answer: Players may respond with more reinforcements until all pass; then resolve using the new totals. Bystanders cannot play reinforcements merely by being present.

clauses: Ordinary per-player flare limit.
Ordinary per-card flare limit and return timing.
When an alien uses its own Wild rather than Super.

answer.text: Ordinary per-player flare limit.
answer.answer: A player may play at most one flare per encounter.

answer.text: Ordinary per-card flare limit and return timing.
answer.answer: An individual flare may be used only once per encounter even if it changes hands. After its effect finishes, return it to hand immediately unless its effect says otherwise.

answer.text: When an alien uses its own Wild rather than Super.
answer.answer: Normally use Wild, but if it is your own alien’s flare and your power is available, you must use Super. If the power is lost or zapped, only Wild is available.

clauses: Offense lacks encounter cards at Start Turn.
Defense lacks encounter cards at Planning.
Offense runs out of encounter cards later in its turn.
Whether offense must play other cards before its starting hand replacement; automatic draws.

answer.text: Offense lacks encounter cards at Start Turn.
answer.answer: Before Regroup effects on the first encounter of its turn, offense reveals and discards its remaining hand and draws eight new cards if it has no encounter cards.

answer.text: Defense lacks encounter cards at Planning.
answer.answer: At Planning, a defense with no encounter cards reveals/discards its remaining hand and draws eight cards, repeating until it has an encounter card.

answer.text: Offense runs out of encounter cards later in its turn.
answer.answer: When offense later needs to play an encounter card but has none, its turn ends instead of drawing a replacement. Offense returns committed ships to its own colonies; each ally returns that ally’s ships to that ally’s colonies, subject to the normal no-colony relocation rule.

answer.text: Whether offense must play other cards before its starting hand replacement; automatic draws.
answer.answer: No. Offense may first play legally playable non-encounter cards but is not required to. There is no automatic draw at encounter/turn end or merely for running out of cards; specific effects may grant draws.

clauses: Whether offense may begin a second encounter without an encounter card and hope to draw one later.
What ends an ordinary turn after its first or second encounter.

answer.text: Whether offense may begin a second encounter without an encounter card and hope to draw one later.
answer.answer: No. An optional second encounter requires at least one encounter card already in offense’s hand; offense cannot start it hoping to get one before Planning.

answer.text: What ends an ordinary turn after its first or second encounter.
answer.answer: After an unsuccessful first encounter, the turn passes left; after a successful first, offense may take an eligible optional second encounter or pass left. After the second encounter, the turn passes left. Machine is an exception.

clauses: When an ordinary alien power is lost and regained based on home colonies, and whether it can be used once more upon loss.
Whether Cosmic Zap stops every printed part of the sheet.

answer.text: When an ordinary alien power is lost and regained based on home colonies, and whether it can be used once more upon loss.
answer.answer: With fewer than three home colonies, immediately turn the sheet facedown and lose the power; it cannot be used one last time. Restore it faceup when the player again occupies at least three home planets. (Masochist is a stated exception.)

answer.text: Whether Cosmic Zap stops every printed part of the sheet.
answer.answer: No. Zap cancels a cancellable use and prevents further uses until the encounter ends; clauses that do not require a power use are not themselves zappable and continue to apply.

clauses: Player order for truly simultaneous contradictory effects.
Whether a player may generally interrupt an effect already resolving with another non-Zap action.
Whether a power can be Cosmic Zapped preemptively.

answer.text: Player order for truly simultaneous contradictory effects.
answer.answer: Resolve offense first, then defense, then other players clockwise starting left of offense; effects with more specific before/after timing take precedence.

answer.text: Whether a player may generally interrupt an effect already resolving with another non-Zap action.
answer.answer: No. Finish one effect before starting another, except a Zap or an effect expressly allowing interruption. Once a hand-targeting effect begins resolving, only a Zap or specific interrupt can intervene.

answer.text: Whether a power can be Cosmic Zapped preemptively.
answer.answer: No. A power may be Cosmic Zapped only when it is being used.

clauses: When ordinary five-foreign-colony victories are checked and whether they can be shared.
Tick-Tock token setup and events that remove a token.
What happens when Tick-Tock loses its last token because a deal gives both main players their fifth foreign colony.

answer.text: When ordinary five-foreign-colony victories are checked and whether they can be shared.
answer.answer: At the very end of Resolution, any player with five current foreign colonies wins; multiple players meeting the condition together share victory.

answer.text: Tick-Tock token setup and events that remove a token.
answer.answer: Tick-Tock starts with ten tokens. Each time any player wins as defense, or any two players make a successful deal, remove one token.

answer.text: What happens when Tick-Tock loses its last token because a deal gives both main players their fifth foreign colony.
answer.answer: When no tokens remain, Tick-Tock immediately wins; it can also win normally. In the stated case the two main players and Tick-Tock share the win.

clauses: Eligible player role, optionality and phase.
Required ship presence and timing relative to card selection/reveal.
Where and how many ships may move.
Whether a shipless winner receives a colony.

answer.text: Eligible player role, optionality and phase.
answer.answer: Amoeba is a main player only; Ooze is optional in Planning.

answer.text: Required ship presence and timing relative to card selection/reveal.
answer.answer: Amoeba must have at least one ship in the encounter. It may use Ooze after encounter cards are selected but before reveal.

answer.text: Where and how many ships may move.
answer.answer: It may remove some or all of its encounter ships to its colonies, or add any number from any of its colonies, even above the normal four-ship maximum. Chosen ships move simultaneously.

answer.text: Whether a shipless winner receives a colony.
answer.answer: No. If Amoeba wins with no ships left in the encounter, it cannot receive a colony.

clauses: Eligible player role, optionality and phase.
Card pairing and outcome.
How ships affect the totals.
Ordinary tie rule.

answer.text: Eligible player role, optionality and phase.
answer.answer: Anti-Matter is a main player only; Negation is mandatory in Reveal.

answer.text: Card pairing and outcome.
answer.answer: After both main players reveal attack cards, Anti-Matter uses Negation to make the lower total win.

answer.text: How ships affect the totals.
answer.answer: Anti-Matter subtracts its own ships and any offensive and defensive allies’ ships from the appropriate side’s attack card. The opposing main player’s total is otherwise calculated normally.

answer.text: Ordinary tie rule.
answer.answer: Defense still wins a tie.

clauses: Eligible player role, optionality and phase.
Trigger and timing relative to compensation.
Who looks at and selects cards, and how many.
What happens to the remaining hand.

answer.text: Eligible player role, optionality and phase.
answer.answer: Barbarian is offense only; Loot and Pillage is mandatory in Resolution.

answer.text: Trigger and timing relative to compensation.
answer.answer: After winning an encounter, Barbarian uses its power before any compensation is collected.

answer.text: Who looks at and selects cards, and how many.
answer.answer: Barbarian takes and looks at the opponent’s hand, then may select up to one card for each of its own ships in the encounter and add those cards to its hand.

answer.text: What happens to the remaining hand.
answer.answer: Barbarian discards the rest of the opponent’s hand.

clauses: Eligible player role, optionality and phase.
When announced and which pairing permits it.
What changes and what stays fixed; calculate attacks 15 and 8.

answer.text: Eligible player role, optionality and phase.
answer.answer: Calculator is a main player only; equalize is optional in Planning.

answer.text: When announced and which pairing permits it.
answer.answer: After cards are selected but before reveal, Calculator may declare equalize; it applies only if both revealed cards are attacks.

answer.text: What changes and what stays fixed; calculate attacks 15 and 8.
answer.answer: Reduce the higher attack by the lower value and leave the lower attack unchanged: 15 becomes 15 − 8 = 7, while 8 stays 8.

clauses: Eligible player role, optionality, phase, frequency and draw.
What happens if none of the three cards are encounter cards.
Replacement or addition allowed when encounter cards are drawn.
Destination of replaced and unused cards.

answer.text: Eligible player role, optionality, phase, frequency and draw.
answer.answer: Chosen is a main player only; Divine Intervention is optional in Reveal and may be used once per encounter, after revealing the encounter cards. Draw three cards from the deck.

answer.text: What happens if none of the three cards are encounter cards.
answer.answer: Discard all three; there is no further effect.

answer.text: Replacement or addition allowed when encounter cards are drawn.
answer.answer: If any drawn card is an encounter card, choose one to replace Chosen’s own revealed card; discard the replaced card. If both the original revealed card and chosen replacement are attacks, Chosen may instead add the drawn card’s value to the revealed attack or replace it as normal.

answer.text: Destination of replaced and unused cards.
answer.answer: The displaced revealed card and all other drawn cards are discarded; the selected replacement is used to resolve the encounter, or its value is added under the attack option.

clauses: Eligible player role, optionality and phase.
When, where and from what citadels may be placed.
Which part requires using the power.
When and how many citadels activate, and the bonus.
What happens after defense wins or loses, including unactivated citadels.

answer.text: Eligible player role, optionality and phase.
answer.answer: Citadel is available to any player; Fortification is optional in Planning.

answer.text: When, where and from what citadels may be placed.
answer.answer: During each player’s turn after destiny is drawn, Citadel may place an attack card from hand faceup next to any planet in any system.

answer.text: Which part requires using the power.
answer.answer: Placing citadels does not require a power use; activating them does.

answer.text: When and how many citadels activate, and the bonus.
answer.answer: If a planet with one or more citadels is attacked, after encounter cards are selected but before reveal, Citadel may activate all citadels on that planet. Their combined value is added to the defense total.

answer.text: What happens after defense wins or loses, including unactivated citadels.
answer.answer: If activated and defense loses, discard the citadels. They stay if defense wins or if they were not activated.

clauses: Eligible player role, optionality and phase.
Timing relative to outcome, compensation and discard; which card and destination.

answer.text: Eligible player role, optionality and phase.
answer.answer: Clone is a main player only; Replicate is optional in Resolution.

answer.text: Timing relative to outcome, compensation and discard; which card and destination.
answer.answer: After the encounter is resolved and any compensation is claimed, Clone may return its own encounter card to its hand instead of discarding it. After Sorcerer switches cards, Clone keeps the card that ends in front of it; a kept card is not discarded and Clone takes precedence over Filch and Fido.

clauses: Eligible player role, optionality and phase.
Trigger, number and who chooses extra ship losses; relation to normal losses.
Whether making a deal is successful, and whether it is a win for Cudgel or Barbarian.
Whether converting a revealed negotiate into attack 42 satisfies Cudgel’s revealed-attack condition.

answer.text: Eligible player role, optionality and phase.
answer.answer: Cudgel is a main player only; Smash is mandatory in Resolution.

answer.text: Trigger, number and who chooses extra ship losses; relation to normal losses.
answer.answer: Smash triggers when Cudgel wins an encounter in which it revealed an attack. The opponent must lose extra ships equal to Cudgel’s own ships in the encounter; the opponent chooses those extra ships. These losses are in addition to normal losses.

answer.text: Whether making a deal is successful, and whether it is a win for Cudgel or Barbarian.
answer.answer: A successful deal is a successful encounter, but it is not a win for Cudgel or Barbarian.

answer.text: Whether converting a revealed negotiate into attack 42 satisfies Cudgel’s revealed-attack condition.
answer.answer: No. A negotiate later converted to an attack does not count as having revealed an attack.

clauses: Eligible player role, optionality and phase.
On whose turns and when Command is used.
Information and choice given by Command.
Destiny handling on Dictator’s own turn or if zapped.

answer.text: Eligible player role, optionality and phase.
answer.answer: Dictator is not offense; Command is mandatory in Destiny.

answer.text: On whose turns and when Command is used.
answer.answer: When another player is offense, Dictator acts before destiny is chosen.

answer.text: Information and choice given by Command.
answer.answer: Dictator takes the destiny deck, looks through it and chooses any card; it is treated as though offense drew that card.

answer.text: Destiny handling on Dictator’s own turn or if zapped.
answer.answer: On Dictator’s own turn, or whenever Dictator is zapped, shuffle the remaining destiny cards and deal one randomly.

clauses: Eligible player role, optionality and phase.
When Fetch acts and which card is offered to whom.
What happens if the offer is refused versus accepted.
What benefit Fido may receive.

answer.text: Eligible player role, optionality and phase.
answer.answer: Fido is any player; Fetch is optional in Resolution.

answer.text: When Fetch acts and which card is offered to whom.
answer.answer: After encounter cards are discarded at the end of the encounter, Fido may retrieve one of those discarded encounter cards and offer it to another player. The FAQ clarifies this must be an actual encounter card played as such, not one discarded by Plague, Fodder or Reserve.

answer.text: What happens if the offer is refused versus accepted.
answer.answer: If refused, Fido may keep the card. If accepted, the other player keeps it.

answer.text: What benefit Fido may receive.
answer.answer: After acceptance, Fido may choose either to retrieve one ship from the warp or draw one card from the deck.

clauses: Eligible role, optionality and phase.
When Theft acts, whose card is taken from where and whose hand receives it.

answer.text: Eligible role, optionality and phase.
answer.answer: Filch is a main player only; Theft is optional in Resolution.

answer.text: When Theft acts, whose card is taken from where and whose hand receives it.
answer.answer: After encounter cards are discarded at the end of the encounter, Filch may retrieve the opponent’s encounter card from the discard pile and add it to Filch’s own hand. After Sorcerer switches cards, take the card that ends before the opponent; Clone’s keeping takes precedence, and Filch versus Fido uses ordinary timing.

clauses: Eligible role, optionality, phase, pairing and timing.
Which hand attacks qualify relative to both revealed attacks.
How many may be discarded and how they affect the total.

answer.text: Eligible role, optionality, phase, pairing and timing.
answer.answer: Fodder is a main player only; Overwhelm is optional in Reveal after both main players reveal attack cards.

answer.text: Which hand attacks qualify relative to both revealed attacks.
answer.answer: Qualifying attacks in Fodder’s hand must be higher than Fodder’s own played attack and lower than the opponent’s played attack.

answer.text: How many may be discarded and how they affect the total.
answer.answer: Fodder may discard any or all qualifying hand attacks in one use, then adds their values to its own total. It chooses all cards for that use at once.

clauses: Eligible role, optionality and phase.
When it acts relative to the opponent’s reveal and what is announced.
What happens if unchallenged.
Challenge result, ship counts and locations, chooser, and subsequent encounter resolution.
Printed incompatible alien.

answer.text: Eligible role, optionality and phase.
answer.answer: Gambler is a main player only; Bluff is optional in Reveal.

answer.text: When it acts relative to the opponent’s reveal and what is announced.
answer.answer: After the opponent reveals, Gambler may keep its own encounter card facedown and state what the card is; Gambler may lie.

answer.text: What happens if unchallenged.
answer.answer: If the opponent does not challenge, resolve the encounter as if Gambler’s statement were true, and put Gambler’s still-facedown card on the bottom of the deck instead of discarding it.

answer.text: Challenge result, ship counts and locations, chooser, and subsequent encounter resolution.
answer.answer: On challenge, reveal Gambler’s card. If Gambler lied, Gambler loses as many ships as it had in the encounter; if truthful, the opponent loses as many ships as the opponent had in the encounter. These penalty ships cannot be encounter ships; the losing player chooses ships under their control outside the encounter. Then resolve normally using the revealed cards.

answer.text: Printed incompatible alien.
answer.answer: The printed restriction says not to use Gambler with Sorcerer.

clauses: Eligible role, optionality and phase.
When and to whom tokens are assigned.
Win/deal and loss/failed-deal branches.
Who chooses penalty ships and which ships are ineligible.

answer.text: Eligible role, optionality and phase.
answer.answer: Grudge is a main player only; Revenge is mandatory in Alliance.

answer.text: When and to whom tokens are assigned.
answer.answer: After alliances form, Grudge gives a token to each player it invited who did not ally with Grudge. A player who initially committed at least one ship to Grudge avoids the token even if those ships later leave.

answer.text: Win/deal and loss/failed-deal branches.
answer.answer: If Grudge wins or makes a deal, each token holder discards the token and loses one ship. If Grudge loses or fails a deal, each token holder discards it and loses four ships.

answer.text: Who chooses penalty ships and which ships are ineligible.
answer.answer: Each token holder chooses their own penalty ships. They cannot be ships used to ally with the other side. If a required non-encounter loss has no eligible outside ships, that player loses none.

clauses: Eligible role, optionality and phase.
When Hacker collects compensation, which hand may be targeted and who looks/chooses.
When Hacker owes compensation, who selects the cards the opponent receives.

answer.text: Eligible role, optionality and phase.
answer.answer: Hacker is a main player only; Hack is optional in Resolution.

answer.text: When Hacker collects compensation, which hand may be targeted and who looks/chooses.
answer.answer: When collecting compensation, Hacker may choose any player’s hand, not only the opponent’s, look through that hand and choose the compensation cards.

answer.text: When Hacker owes compensation, who selects the cards the opponent receives.
answer.answer: If an opponent collects compensation from Hacker, Hacker may select the cards that opponent gets.

clauses: Eligible role, optionality and phase.
When Rage acts and what Hate discards.
Other players’ alternatives and attack threshold.
What happens if Hate then lacks encounter cards.

answer.text: Eligible role, optionality and phase.
answer.answer: Hate is offense only; Rage is mandatory at Start Turn.

answer.text: When Rage acts and what Hate discards.
answer.answer: At the start of its own turn, Hate first chooses and discards a card from its hand, then uses Rage.

answer.text: Other players’ alternatives and attack threshold.
answer.answer: Each other player must either discard a card of the same type or lose three ships to warp chosen by Hate. If Hate discarded an attack, the other attack must be equal or higher in value; a player with no qualifying card (or who declines) discards nothing and loses the ships.

answer.text: What happens if Hate then lacks encounter cards.
answer.answer: If after using Rage Hate has no encounter cards in hand, it draws a new hand. A required new starting hand is drawn before Rage.

clauses: Eligible role, optionality and phases.
Qualifying event, whose losses, number returned and destination.
Card benefit and multiple players.
Whether healing removes compensation.

answer.text: Eligible role, optionality and phases.
answer.answer: Healer may act as any player; Heal is optional in Start Turn, Regroup, Destiny, Launch, Alliance, Planning, Reveal or Resolution.

answer.text: Qualifying event, whose losses, number returned and destination.
answer.answer: When another player loses ships to the warp or has ships removed from the game, Healer may return all ships just lost to that player; the healed player places them on any of their colonies. Healer cannot heal itself.

answer.text: Card benefit and multiple players.
answer.answer: Healer earns one deck card for each player healed and may heal several players during an encounter.

answer.text: Whether healing removes compensation.
answer.answer: No. Ships reach the warp before being healed, so healing does not prevent compensation.

clauses: Eligible role, optionality and phase.
Timing and bonus.
What happens if this use is zapped.

answer.text: Eligible role, optionality and phase.
answer.answer: Human may act as a main player or ally; Humanity is mandatory in Reveal.

answer.text: Timing and bonus.
answer.answer: After encounter cards are revealed, Human adds 4 to its own side’s total.

answer.text: What happens if this use is zapped.
answer.answer: If the use is zapped, Human’s side automatically wins, even if one or both players revealed negotiate.

clauses: Eligible role, optionality and phase.
Timing, ship limit/source and cards drawn.
What happens if the use is zapped.

answer.text: Eligible role, optionality and phase.
answer.answer: Kamikaze is a main player only; Sacrifice is optional in Planning.

answer.text: Timing, ship limit/source and cards drawn.
answer.answer: Before encounter cards are selected, Kamikaze may send up to four of its own ships from any of its colonies to the warp, drawing two deck cards per ship. Choose and sacrifice all ships for the use together before drawing.

answer.text: What happens if the use is zapped.
answer.answer: The sacrificed ships are not lost to the warp if the power use is zapped.

clauses: Eligible role, optionality and phase; declaration timing.
Card-selection restriction.
How and when the outcome changes, including zapped Human.

answer.text: Eligible role, optionality and phase; declaration timing.
answer.answer: Loser is a main player only; Upset is optional in Planning and must be declared before encounter cards are selected.

answer.text: Card-selection restriction.
answer.answer: After Upset is declared, both main players must play attack cards if they can.

answer.text: How and when the outcome changes, including zapped Human.
answer.answer: After reveal, the normally winning side loses and the losing side wins. This reversal happens after all other game effects resolve, including Human’s power being zapped.

clauses: Eligible role, optionality and phase.
What outcomes permit another encounter, maximum encounter count and hand requirement.

answer.text: Eligible role, optionality and phase.
answer.answer: Machine is offense only; Continuity is optional in Resolution.

answer.text: What outcomes permit another encounter, maximum encounter count and hand requirement.
answer.answer: After completing an encounter, whether successful or not, Machine may take another encounter if at least one encounter card remains in its hand. There is no two-encounter cap; the hand-card requirement remains for each next encounter.

clauses: Eligible role, optionality and phases.
Timing for the launch/ally limit versus ship-strength effect.
One-ship limit and whether it applies to defense.
Ship value for encounter total versus compensation/rewards.
How a Macron ship counts for an effect specifying a number of ships, such as Virus.

answer.text: Eligible role, optionality and phases.
answer.answer: Macron may act as a main player or ally; Mass is mandatory in Launch, Alliance and Reveal.

answer.text: Timing for the launch/ally limit versus ship-strength effect.
answer.answer: As offense, Macron uses the launch effect before launching ships; as an ally, after allies are invited. As a main player or ally, the ship-strength effect is used after encounter cards are revealed (retained official erratum).

answer.text: One-ship limit and whether it applies to defense.
answer.answer: As offense or ally, Macron may send only one ship into the encounter. This does not impose a one-ship limit on Macron when defending as a main player.

answer.text: Ship value for encounter total versus compensation/rewards.
answer.answer: Each Macron ship adds 4 to its side’s encounter total. When collecting compensation or rewards, each physical ship counts as two ships.

answer.text: How a Macron ship counts for an effect specifying a number of ships, such as Virus.
answer.answer: It counts as one physical ship, not four; only Macron’s explicit encounter strength is four per ship, and the explicit compensation/reward multiplier is two.

clauses: Eligible role, optionality, phase and timing of Hurt Yourself.
Which lost-ship locations count and alternate win condition.
Power maintenance and normal victory eligibility.
Whether an explicit immediate win waits until end of Resolution, and what can interrupt it.

answer.text: Eligible role, optionality, phase and timing of Hurt Yourself.
answer.answer: Masochist acts as any player; Hurt Yourself is mandatory at the start of any player’s Regroup, before offense retrieves a warp ship.

answer.text: Which lost-ship locations count and alternate win condition.
answer.answer: Masochist wins if all its ships have been lost, including ships in the warp, removed from the game or captured by other players.

answer.text: Power maintenance and normal victory eligibility.
answer.answer: Masochist does not lose its power for having too few home colonies and may still win normally.

answer.text: Whether an explicit immediate win waits until end of Resolution, and what can interrupt it.
answer.answer: No. An explicit immediate win ends the game when that effect resolves. It can be stopped if zapped or specifically interrupted before resolution.

clauses: Eligible role, optionality, phase and timing.
Whose hand may be inspected and main-player restriction.
What Mind may reveal to others.

answer.text: Eligible role, optionality, phase and timing.
answer.answer: Mind may act as any player; Knowledge is optional in Alliance before allies are invited.

answer.text: Whose hand may be inspected and main-player restriction.
answer.answer: Mind may inspect the entire hand of one main player. If Mind is a main player, it may inspect only the opponent’s hand; as another player, it may choose either main player.

answer.text: What Mind may reveal to others.
answer.answer: Mind may not tell any other player what cards it saw. The FAQ also clarifies Mind cannot inspect Miser’s hoard.

clauses: Eligible role, optionality, phase and timing.
Which cards are changed and how digits are treated.
Requested values.

answer.text: Eligible role, optionality, phase and timing.
answer.answer: Mirror is a main player only; Reversal is optional in Planning after encounter cards are selected but before reveal.

answer.text: Which cards are changed and how digits are treated.
answer.answer: Reverse the digits of any attack cards revealed in the encounter; other card types are unchanged.

answer.text: Requested values.
answer.answer: 15 becomes 51, 20 becomes 02, and 08 becomes 80.

clauses: Eligible role, optionality, phases and setup hands/choice.
How Hoard substitutes for the ordinary hand.
Whether gained cards may be put in hoard or others inspect/draw from it.
When and how the hoard can be replaced.

answer.text: Eligible role, optionality, phases and setup hands/choice.
answer.answer: Miser may act as any player; Hoard is optional in Start Turn, Regroup, Destiny, Launch, Alliance, Planning, Reveal and Resolution. At setup, deal Miser two separate eight-card hands; Miser looks at both and chooses one as the facedown hoard on its sheet.

answer.text: How Hoard substitutes for the ordinary hand.
answer.answer: Whenever Miser wants to play a card, it may use Hoard to play from the hoard instead of the normal hand.

answer.text: Whether gained cards may be put in hoard or others inspect/draw from it.
answer.answer: No. Miser cannot add gained cards to the hoard, and other players may not look at or draw cards from it.

answer.text: When and how the hoard can be replaced.
answer.answer: If the hoard has no encounter cards, Miser may reveal and discard it, then receive a new eight-card hoard.

clauses: Eligible role, optionality, phase, timing and defense hand-size threshold.
Defense’s two choices and how discards occur.
Ships and encounter result under each choice.

answer.text: Eligible role, optionality, phase, timing and defense hand-size threshold.
answer.answer: Mite is offense only; Bluster is mandatory in Launch before allies are invited, if defense has more than three cards.

answer.text: Defense’s two choices and how discards occur.
answer.answer: Defense must either discard down to three cards at random or let Mite establish a colony on the targeted world.

answer.text: Ships and encounter result under each choice.
answer.answer: If defense grants the colony, Mite lands any of its own ships in the gate on the target; they coexist with defense ships, which do not go to the warp, and the encounter immediately ends successfully. If defense discards to three, the encounter continues normally.

clauses: Eligible role, optionality, phase and hand threshold/timing.
Sources, sequence, randomness and stopping point for cards.

answer.text: Eligible role, optionality, phase and hand threshold/timing.
answer.answer: Mutant is a main player only; Regenerate is optional in Alliance before allies are invited, if Mutant has fewer than eight cards.

answer.text: Sources, sequence, randomness and stopping point for cards.
answer.answer: Draw cards one at a time at random from any player or players, or the deck, until Mutant’s hand is full at eight cards.

clauses: Eligible roles and whose ships Protect covers in each role.
Timing, loss destination and where protected ships return.

answer.text: Eligible roles and whose ships Protect covers in each role.
answer.answer: Observer may act as a main player or ally; Protect is mandatory in Resolution. As an ally it protects Observer’s own ships. As a main player it protects the ships of Observer’s allies.

answer.text: Timing, loss destination and where protected ships return.
answer.answer: When the protected ships would be lost to the warp during Resolution, instead return them to colonies of their owners’ choice. As an ally this covers all Observer’s ships, including those outside the encounter; as a main player it covers all its allies’ ships, including remote losses. It does not prevent Void eradication.

clauses: Eligible role, optionality, phase and timing.
Whose card is played first and how.
When Oracle selects and plays its own card.

answer.text: Eligible role, optionality, phase and timing.
answer.answer: Oracle is a main player only; Foresee is mandatory in Planning before encounter cards are selected.

answer.text: Whose card is played first and how.
answer.answer: Oracle forces the opponent to select and play an encounter card faceup first.

answer.text: When Oracle selects and plays its own card.
answer.answer: Only after seeing the opponent’s card does Oracle select and play its own encounter card.

clauses: Eligible role, optionality and phase.
Pairing that triggers Peace and winner.
What happens if both reveal negotiate.

answer.text: Eligible role, optionality and phase.
answer.answer: Pacifist is a main player only; Peace is mandatory in Reveal.

answer.text: Pairing that triggers Peace and winner.
answer.answer: If Pacifist reveals negotiate against an opponent’s attack, Pacifist uses Peace to win the encounter.

answer.text: What happens if both reveal negotiate.
answer.answer: They attempt a deal as usual.

clauses: Eligible role, optionality and phase.
When and which invitation/side choices Infest changes, and ships sent.
Whether it overrides an effect specifically preventing alliance.

answer.text: Eligible role, optionality and phase.
answer.answer: Parasite is not a main player; Infest is optional in Alliance.

answer.text: When and which invitation/side choices Infest changes, and ships sent.
answer.answer: When Parasite’s turn to ally comes, it may ally with either side as though invited, even if it was not invited, sending one to four ships as usual.

answer.text: Whether it overrides an effect specifically preventing alliance.
answer.answer: No. It cannot bypass a game effect that specifically prevents alliance, such as Force Field.

clauses: Eligible role, optionality and phase.
When, how many cards from where, and to which recipient.
When recipient may use the card.
Condition for drawing a new hand.

answer.text: Eligible role, optionality and phase.
answer.answer: Philanthropist may be a main player or ally; Giving is optional in Alliance.

answer.text: When, how many cards from where, and to which recipient.
answer.answer: After alliances form, it may give one card from its hand to either main player. If Philanthropist is a main player, it must give the card to the opponent.

answer.text: When recipient may use the card.
answer.answer: The recipient immediately adds the card to hand and may play it normally.

answer.text: Condition for drawing a new hand.
answer.answer: If afterward Philanthropist has no encounter cards in hand and is a main player, it draws a new hand. An ally does not meet the role condition.

clauses: Eligible role, optionality and phase; results that trigger Reincarnation.
Replacement source and rejected candidates.
What happens on later losses and what old power remains.
Which powers a copying alien may copy and consequence of its loss.

answer.text: Eligible role, optionality and phase; results that trigger Reincarnation.
answer.answer: Reincarnator may be a main player or ally; Reincarnation is mandatory in Resolution when it loses an encounter or fails a deal.

answer.text: Replacement source and rejected candidates.
answer.answer: Draw an alien power at random from the unused pile and become that alien. Redraw if it has Game Setup text or is not allowed in the current game.

answer.text: What happens on later losses and what old power remains.
answer.answer: If Reincarnator loses a later encounter, discard the current alien and draw a new one. Reincarnator keeps its Reincarnator power while using the replacement power.

answer.text: Which powers a copying alien may copy and consequence of its loss.
answer.answer: An alien able to copy powers may copy both Reincarnator and the currently reincarnated power. If that copying alien loses an encounter, it must reincarnate and loses its original power.

clauses: Eligible role, optionality and phases.
Ship retrieval event, quantity, source/destination and restriction.
Card draw event, quantity and source.

answer.text: Eligible role, optionality and phases.
answer.answer: Remora may act as any player; Cling is optional in Start Turn, Regroup, Destiny, Launch, Alliance, Planning, Reveal or Resolution.

answer.text: Ship retrieval event, quantity, source/destination and restriction.
answer.answer: Whenever another player retrieves one or more ships from the warp, Remora may retrieve one of its own ships from the warp to its colonies. It may not retrieve a ship in the same encounter in which that ship entered the warp.

answer.text: Card draw event, quantity and source.
answer.answer: Whenever another player draws one or more cards, Remora may draw one card from the cosmic deck.

clauses: Eligible role, optionality and phase.
When, which attack cards and values, and number.
Cost and destination when canceling another player’s reinforcement.

answer.text: Eligible role, optionality and phase.
answer.answer: Reserve may be a main player or ally; Reinforce is optional in Reveal.

answer.text: When, which attack cards and values, and number.
answer.answer: After encounter cards are revealed, Reserve may play one or more attack cards from hand with value 06 or less as reinforcements of their printed values; the FAQ says choose all cards for one use together.

answer.text: Cost and destination when canceling another player’s reinforcement.
answer.answer: When another player plays a reinforcement, Reserve may use its power and discard a negotiate card to cancel and discard that reinforcement. If Reserve is zapped as it is about to play an attack, it keeps that attack card.

clauses: Eligible role, optionality and phase.
Qualifying destiny draws and whose ship is selected from where.
Wild destiny and whether target must be offense’s chosen defense.

answer.text: Eligible role, optionality and phase.
answer.answer: Shadow acts as any player; Execute is mandatory in Destiny.

answer.text: Qualifying destiny draws and whose ship is selected from where.
answer.answer: Whenever another player’s color or a special destiny targeting another player is drawn, Shadow chooses one ship belonging to that player from any colony of Shadow’s choice and sends it to the warp. The FAQ says this occurs for each qualifying destiny card drawn, even one later discarded/redrawn.

answer.text: Wild destiny and whether target must be offense’s chosen defense.
answer.answer: On a wild destiny, Shadow may execute one ship belonging to any other player, regardless of whom offense chooses to attack; the target need not be the chosen defense.

clauses: Eligible role, optionality and phase.
When Magic acts and what is switched.
Which card each player reveals afterward.

answer.text: Eligible role, optionality and phase.
answer.answer: Sorcerer is a main player only; Magic is optional in Planning.

answer.text: When Magic acts and what is switched.
answer.answer: After encounter cards are selected but before reveal, Sorcerer may switch its encounter card with the opponent’s.

answer.text: Which card each player reveals afterward.
answer.answer: After the switch, the opponent reveals Sorcerer’s original card, and Sorcerer reveals the opponent’s original card.

clauses: Eligible role, optionality and phase.
Required pairing, losing margin and role; application to low-total-wins encounters.
Ships that escape loss and landing destination.
Coexistence limits.

answer.text: Eligible role, optionality and phase.
answer.answer: Spiff is offense only; Crash Land is optional in Resolution.

answer.text: Required pairing, losing margin and role; application to low-total-wins encounters.
answer.answer: When offense loses an encounter in which both main players revealed attack cards, and offense lost by 10 or more, it may use Crash Land. The retained erratum includes low-total-wins encounters.

answer.text: Ships that escape loss and landing destination.
answer.answer: Spiff may land one of its own ships that would otherwise go to the warp on the winning defensive planet.

answer.text: Coexistence limits.
answer.answer: The ship coexists with ships already there, unless the location or an alien’s rule prohibits coexistence.

clauses: Eligible role, optionality and phase.
Token setup and the two token-removing events.
Final token and normal win.

answer.text: Eligible role, optionality and phase.
answer.answer: Tick-Tock may act as any player; Patience is mandatory in Resolution.

answer.text: Token setup and the two token-removing events.
answer.answer: Set up ten tokens. Remove one whenever any player wins as defense, and remove one whenever any two players make a successful deal.

answer.text: Final token and normal win.
answer.answer: When no tokens remain, Tick-Tock immediately wins. It may also win normally.

clauses: Eligible role, optionality and phase.
When hands are exchanged and which hand each keeps.

answer.text: Eligible role, optionality and phase.
answer.answer: Trader is a main player only; Transference is optional in Planning.

answer.text: When hands are exchanged and which hand each keeps.
answer.answer: Before encounter cards are selected, Trader may trade hands with the opponent. They exchange hands and each keeps the newly received hand.

clauses: Eligible role, optionality, phase and required card.
Value rule and rounding.
Results for attacks 10 and 11.

answer.text: Eligible role, optionality, phase and required card.
answer.answer: Tripler is a main player only; Thrice is mandatory in Reveal after Tripler reveals an attack.

answer.text: Value rule and rounding.
answer.answer: An attack of 10 or less is tripled. An attack above 10 is divided by three and rounded up.

answer.text: Results for attacks 10 and 11.
answer.answer: Attack 10 becomes 10 × 3 = 30. Attack 11 becomes ceil(11 ÷ 3) = 4.

clauses: Eligible role, optionality, phases and triggering event.
How many additional ships may be lost.
Who chooses affected players and quantities versus colony sources.
Whether Vacuum may target itself and whether losses are additional.

answer.text: Eligible role, optionality, phases and triggering event.
answer.answer: Vacuum acts as any player; Catharsis is mandatory in Start Turn, Regroup, Destiny, Launch, Alliance, Planning, Reveal and Resolution. It triggers whenever Vacuum’s own ships are lost to the warp.

answer.text: How many additional ships may be lost.
answer.answer: Vacuum may take up to as many additional ships as its own ships lost to the warp.

answer.text: Who chooses affected players and quantities versus colony sources.
answer.answer: Vacuum specifies which other players are affected and how many ships each must lose. Each targeted player chooses the colony or colonies those ships come from.

answer.text: Whether Vacuum may target itself and whether losses are additional.
answer.answer: Vacuum cannot target itself. These losses are in addition to ordinary encounter losses.

clauses: Eligible role, optionality, phase and timing.
How own ships and attack value are combined; treatment of allied ships.
Calculate attack 8, three own ships, two allied ships.

answer.text: Eligible role, optionality, phase and timing.
answer.answer: Virus is a main player only; Multiply is mandatory in Reveal after Virus reveals an attack.

answer.text: How own ships and attack value are combined; treatment of allied ships.
answer.answer: Multiply Virus’s own encounter ships by its attack-card value instead of adding them; add allies’ ships normally.

answer.text: Calculate attack 8, three own ships, two allied ships.
answer.answer: Virus’s own ships contribute 3 × 8 = 24; add the two allied ships normally, for a total of 26 before any other modifiers.

clauses: Eligible role, optionality, phase and triggering result.
Whose ships go to which destination.
Protected minimum and destination of excess losses.
Apply the limit to an opponent with six ships who would lose three.

answer.text: Eligible role, optionality, phase and triggering result.
answer.answer: Void is a main player only; Eradicate is mandatory in Resolution when Void wins an encounter.

answer.text: Whose ships go to which destination.
answer.answer: Void removes the losing side’s ships from the game instead of sending them to the warp, subject to the minimum-survivors limit.

answer.text: Protected minimum and destination of excess losses.
answer.answer: A player cannot be reduced below five surviving ships, the number needed for five foreign colonies. Any would-be eradication below that limit goes to the warp instead.

answer.text: Apply the limit to an opponent with six ships who would lose three.
answer.answer: Only one of the three can be eradicated: that leaves five surviving. The other two go to the warp.

clauses: Eligible role, optionality and phases.
Whose discarded artifacts trigger Salvage and whether played status matters.
Whether Vulch may salvage its own played artifacts.
Hand-refresh reveal, retention and new-draw procedure.

answer.text: Eligible role, optionality and phases.
answer.answer: Vulch acts as any player; Salvage is mandatory in Start Turn, Regroup, Destiny, Launch, Alliance, Planning, Reveal and Resolution.

answer.text: Whose discarded artifacts trigger Salvage and whether played status matters.
answer.answer: Any other player’s discarded artifact triggers Salvage, whether it was played or not.

answer.text: Whether Vulch may salvage its own played artifacts.
answer.answer: No. Vulch’s own played artifacts are discarded normally and cannot be salvaged.

answer.text: Hand-refresh reveal, retention and new-draw procedure.
answer.answer: When drawing a new hand, Vulch reveals and retains its old artifacts, then draws eight new cards in addition to those retained artifacts.

clauses: Eligible role, optionality, phase and required revealed card.
Which warp ships count and the amount added.

answer.text: Eligible role, optionality, phase and required revealed card.
answer.answer: Warpish is a main player only; Necromancy is mandatory in Reveal after it reveals an attack.

answer.text: Which warp ships count and the amount added.
answer.answer: Count every ship in the warp, regardless of owner, and add one to Warpish’s total for each ship. Count ships present when the power is used; later arrivals do not retroactively add to it.

clauses: Eligible role, optionality, phase, results and token quantities for experience.
When/how combat bonus is used, card requirement and token spending.
Whether a zap prevents experience gain.

answer.text: Eligible role, optionality, phase, results and token quantities for experience.
answer.answer: Warrior is a main player only; Mastery is mandatory in Reveal. After an encounter in which Warrior was a main player, gain one token for a win or deal, and two for a loss or failed deal.

answer.text: When/how combat bonus is used, card requirement and token spending.
answer.answer: As a main player after revealing an attack, Warrior adds one to its total per sheet token. Tokens are not spent.

answer.text: Whether a zap prevents experience gain.
answer.answer: No. Gaining experience does not require a power use and continues if the combat bonus is zapped.

clauses: Eligible role, optionality, corrected phase and timing.
How it can change opponent and location; third-player-system colony condition.
Whether other effects of drawn destiny still occur.

answer.text: Eligible role, optionality, corrected phase and timing.
answer.answer: Will is offense only; Choice is mandatory in Destiny, after drawing destiny (the official correction moves it from the printed Launch timing).

answer.text: How it can change opponent and location; third-player-system colony condition.
answer.answer: Will may choose any alien on any planet to encounter instead of the one dictated by destiny. It may choose another player’s colony in a third player’s system only if that colony actually exists; it may still encounter a home-system owner on that owner’s empty home planet.

answer.text: Whether other effects of drawn destiny still occur.
answer.answer: Yes. Other effects caused by the drawn destiny, including Shadow, still occur.

clauses: Eligible role, optionality, phases and ordinary warp-loss prevention.
Additional deal clause and whether it requires a power use.
Who may be freed, destination and numerical limit.

answer.text: Eligible role, optionality, phases and ordinary warp-loss prevention.
answer.answer: Zombie acts as any player; Immortality is mandatory in Start Turn, Regroup, Destiny, Launch, Alliance, Planning, Reveal and Resolution. Whenever Zombie’s ships should be lost to the warp, it returns them to any of its colonies instead, where they remain in use.

answer.text: Additional deal clause and whether it requires a power use.
answer.answer: As part of its deal, Zombie may free ships from the warp; this clause does not require a power use.

answer.text: Who may be freed, destination and numerical limit.
answer.answer: FAQ limits liberation to Zombie’s negotiating opponent, not a third player. Return the freed ships to any existing colonies that opponent has. There is no numerical limit.

clauses: Procedure when a needed cosmic-deck draw finds both deck and discard empty.
What happens if that still cannot provide full hands, including Miser’s hoard and other setup holdings.

answer.text: Procedure when a needed cosmic-deck draw finds both deck and discard empty.
answer.answer: When a needed draw cannot be made because both deck and discard are empty, Cosmic Quake makes everyone discard their hands; shuffle and deal eight cards to each player.

answer.text: What happens if that still cannot provide full hands, including Miser’s hoard and other setup holdings.
answer.answer: Cosmic Aftershock gathers all cosmic cards, including Miser’s hoard and other set-aside cards, shuffles them, and replenishes the card holdings from Game Setup, including Miser’s hoard.

clauses: Whether Zombie-prevented or Void-eradicated ships earn negotiate compensation.
Whether Zombie qualifies if zapped ships actually enter the warp.

answer.text: Whether Zombie-prevented or Void-eradicated ships earn negotiate compensation.
answer.answer: No. Zombie ships prevented from reaching the warp and Void-eradicated ships do not earn compensation.

answer.text: Whether Zombie qualifies if zapped ships actually enter the warp.
answer.answer: Yes. If Zombie is zapped and the ships actually reach the warp, compensation can apply, assuming the other attack-versus-negotiate requirements are met.

clauses: Distinguish losing ships, ships lost to the warp and ships sent to the warp.
Can a losing Zombie ship avoid becoming lost?
Do ships sent by a separate effect count as lost?

answer.text: Distinguish losing ships, ships lost to the warp and ships sent to the warp.
answer.answer: “Losing ships” are encounter participants that should suffer defeat’s loss. Ships “lost to warp” actually arrive involuntarily at some point during the encounter. Ships “sent” reach the warp through a specific action/effect, sometimes voluntarily, while not directly involved in the encounter; they count as lost rather than encounter-losing ships. If an interruption prevents arrival, there is no actual warp loss.

answer.text: Can a losing Zombie ship avoid becoming lost?
answer.answer: Yes. Zombie prevents its own ships from reaching the warp and returns them to its colonies; prevented ships are not ships actually lost to the warp.

answer.text: Do ships sent by a separate effect count as lost?
answer.answer: Yes. Ships sent to the warp by a separate effect count as lost, though they are not encounter-losing ships.

clauses: Whether a reinforcement may be legally played before compensation starts to remove it from hand.
Whether you may dump cards after Hacker has targeted your hand.
What can interrupt the hand-targeting action.

answer.text: Whether a reinforcement may be legally played before compensation starts to remove it from hand.
answer.answer: A card may be legally played before compensation starts, but the reinforcement must be played during its legal Reveal window; the passed window cannot be reopened later just to discard it.

answer.text: Whether you may dump cards after Hacker has targeted your hand.
answer.answer: No. Once Hacker’s hand-targeting effect begins resolving, you cannot dump reinforcements after Reveal has passed.

answer.text: What can interrupt the hand-targeting action.
answer.answer: Only a Cosmic Zap or a specific effect that permits interruption can interrupt a resolving hand-targeting effect.

clauses: Where Mobius Tubes sends released ships if their owner has no colonies.
Extra placement offense may make first.

answer.text: Where Mobius Tubes sends released ships if their owner has no colonies.
answer.answer: Return released ships to the warp if no colony can receive them.

answer.text: Extra placement offense may make first.
answer.answer: Before the remaining released ships return to the warp, offense may place up to four of its released ships in the gate.

clauses: Whether Start Turn occurs on both encounters or only the first.
Order between offense’s needed new hand and a Regroup Plague.

answer.text: Whether Start Turn occurs on both encounters or only the first.
answer.answer: Start Turn occurs only before the first encounter of a turn.

answer.text: Order between offense’s needed new hand and a Regroup Plague.
answer.answer: The offense replaces its encounter-less hand at Start Turn before Regroup effects, so it draws the new hand before the Regroup Plague.

clauses: Order for non-encounter discards when discard order matters.
Order of main-player encounter-card discards and which ends on top.

answer.text: Order for non-encounter discards when discard order matters.
answer.answer: Discard non-encounter cards first in alphabetical/numerical order.

answer.text: Order of main-player encounter-card discards and which ends on top.
answer.answer: Then discard encounter cards starting with offense, continuing clockwise, and ending with defense; the defense’s encounter card is on top.

clauses: Phase through which an empty home-planet reclamation proceeds.
Whether reclamation is a win and successful encounter.
Whether Warrior earns experience for reclamation.
Number of ships and eligible holdings for placement.

answer.text: Phase through which an empty home-planet reclamation proceeds.
answer.answer: It proceeds only through Launch.

answer.text: Whether reclamation is a win and successful encounter.
answer.answer: Yes. It counts as both a win and a successful encounter.

answer.text: Whether Warrior earns experience for reclamation.
answer.answer: Yes. Warrior earns experience because reclaiming the empty home planet counts as a win.

answer.text: Number of ships and eligible holdings for placement.
answer.answer: Offense may move up to four ships from any of its other existing home or foreign colonies onto the empty home planet.

E1.text:
## Overview

This summary covers the original **Fantasy Flight English 2008 CE01** game for 3–5 players, including its fifty original aliens, normal flare system and applicable official FAQ rulings. Optional Technology, Four Planets, Hidden Powers, Rotating Powers and Freewheeling Flares are excluded, as are Anniversary bonus content and all expansions. Read an individual card's printed effect and timing when playing it; the flare rules below explain the shared system rather than reproduce every flare card.

Each player leads an alien trying to establish five **foreign colonies**. A colony is one or more ships of one color on one planet; extra ships on that planet do not make extra colonies. Several colors can coexist there, each with its own colony. Home colonies are in your own system; foreign colonies are outside it. Five foreign planets can all be in one other system. Alien powers override conflicting general rules.

E2.text:
## Setup

1. Put the warp in the center. Each player takes five planets of one color, places four of their twenty ships on each, and places their colony marker beside the warp's 0 space.
2. Remove destiny cards naming unused player colors; shuffle the rest, including wilds and specials.
3. Shuffle the flares, deal two to each player, and give them the matching alien sheets. Each secretly chooses one alien, initially placing it facedown, and returns the other sheet to the box. This is the standard selection procedure; Hidden Powers is a separate excluded variant. The original text does not specify when standard-game sheets are turned faceup; unlike the optional Hidden Powers rule, it gives no explicit reveal window. This source gap is recorded rather than supplying a new setup rule. Green/yellow/red indicate recommended experience, not strength. Beginners may start with green aliens without flares.
4. Add **both flares dealt to every player**, including rejected aliens' flares, to the cosmic deck. Add random extras if needed to reach ten flares total; shuffle. Deal eight-card hands. Keep card faces private unless an effect allows showing them.
5. Draw destiny until a player color appears; that player starts. Shuffle the drawn card back into the destiny deck. Play passes left thereafter.

Apply printed alien Game Setup instructions as well. If chosen aliens have a printed incompatibility, remove the alien bearing the restriction, keeping the unrestricted alien. Its player may use their originally rejected alien or draw a replacement unused flare and take that alien, redrawing conflicts. Gambler's printed restriction is **Do not use with Sorcerer**; using them together is an optional FAQ-permitted relaxation, outside this standard setup.

E3.text:
### 1. Regroup

Offense must retrieve one of its ships from the warp if available, placing it on any existing home or foreign colony. The original rulebook puts this retrieved ship directly in the gate if offense has no colonies. The FAQ adds that a player who has no colonies or ships on their turn may instead place the Regroup ship on any home planet. Ordinary relocation with no colony to receive ships sends them to the warp; the stated Regroup exceptions take precedence.

E4.text:
### 2. Destiny

Draw destiny to determine the defense and target system. **When only one card remains, do not draw it**: shuffle it with the destiny discards, then draw from the new deck.

- Another player's color: encounter that player in their home system.
- Your own color: redraw, or target one chosen foreign colony in your home system, making its owner the defense. Other colonies there are bystanders. You can instead aim at a home planet with **no ships of any color**, moving up to four of your ships from any of your other existing home or foreign colonies onto that empty home planet to reclaim it automatically. This counts as a win and successful encounter, proceeds only through Launch, and can qualify you for a second encounter.
- Wild: choose another player and encounter them in their home system.
- Special: follow its conditions, defense and location. The original rulebook's illustrated special card chooses the other player with the most current foreign colonies, excluding offense. Break a tie toward offense's left, choosing the first tied eligible player there; encounter that player in their home system (rulebook p7). For color-dependent effects such as Shadow, treat it as the designated defense's color. If a special card designates you as the defense, the original rulebook also permits trying to drive out a foreign colony in your home system: choose one other player's colony as the defense; all other colonies are unaffected bystanders.

Destiny hazard symbols have no effect in this base game. Ordinarily you cannot attack a player's foreign colony in a third player's system: a color/wild/special targets its defense in that player's home system, while your own color permits driving out a foreign colony in your own system. If you already have colonies on **all planets in the defensive system**, draw destiny again.

E5.text:
### 3. Launch

The offense chooses one planet in the destiny-indicated system and aims the gate at it. Place one to four offense ships on the **wide end of the hyperspace gate**, drawn from any combination of the offense's existing home and foreign colonies. You may strip a colony, but removing its last ship immediately eliminates it. Ships returning from an encounter or warp cannot return to that now-empty location as though it remained your colony.

Defense cannot add or subtract ships on the target. The owner of a home system defends their planet even with zero ships there. Other colors' colonies are **bystanders**: they add nothing to the defense and the encounter result does not harm them. When driving out a foreign colony, target only that one color's colony; all other colors are bystanders.

If you cannot put any ship in the gate or the last offensive ship is removed, continue the encounter. Winning alone does not give offense a colony without a ship to land, unless a specific effect allows it.

E6.text:
### 4. Alliance

Offense names invited allies first; they wait to answer. Defense then invites allies, possibly including the same players. Neither main player may invite the other. Starting with the player left of offense and proceeding clockwise, each other player accepts one invitation or declines all, then commits ships before the next player decides. You may join only one side or neither; normally an invitation is required.

Each ally contributes one to four ships from any of their colonies. Offensive allies place them on the gate; defensive allies place them beside the target planet, **not on it**. The FAQ nevertheless considers defensive allies in the gate for effects referring to that location. Parasite changes invitation eligibility.

E7.text:
### Attack against attack

Each side's total is its main player's attack value plus all ships on its side: offense and offensive allies in the gate; defense on the target plus defensive allies beside it. Higher total wins; **defense wins ties**. Powers and played cards may change this calculation or the winner.

- **Offense wins:** all offense and offensive ally ships land on the target, establishing or reinforcing each color's colony. Defense and defensive ally ships go to warp. Bystanders survive. Advance a colony marker only for a newly established foreign colony, not reinforcement of an existing colony.
- **Defense wins:** defending and bystander colonies stay. Offense and offensive allies go to warp. Defensive allies return their committed ships to any existing own colonies, even different origins; helping defend does not grant a colony on the defended planet. Each defensive ally must collect **one defender reward per ship contributed**. For each contributed ship, draw one cosmic-deck card or retrieve one own warp ship to any own colony; combine these choices freely. The ordinary rule does not permit declining these rewards. Declare the full mix of card draws and warp-ship retrievals **before taking any rewards**; do not inspect an initial draw before deciding the remaining sources (official FAQ p8's base-relevant reward-source rule).

E8.text:
### Attack against negotiate: compensation

The negotiate player automatically loses; resolve the winner's ship destinations normally. The losing main player randomly takes one card from the opponent's hand for each of **their own ships actually lost to the warp**. Exclude allied losses: allies receive no compensation. If the opponent lacks sufficient cards, take the entire hand. Cards are taken without seeing their faces. For random hand-card selection, including compensation, you may see which card backs you select; “at random” means without seeing card faces (FAQ p5). Compensation is stolen hand cards; defender rewards are deck draws and/or warp retrieval.

No compensation for ships prevented from reaching the warp (Zombie/Observer) or removed by Void. Healer returning ships **after** they enter the warp does not remove compensation eligibility. Special winners such as Human/Pacifist can change who wins; compensation still requires the relevant attack-versus-negotiate condition.
